claims.text: The design review's challenges table has five rows: web search engines (ADR 0017), why no search engine (estimate, drivers, ADR 0030 reopen condition), large shop moving under ADR 0026, slowing orders at a peak, caching popular searches.
In the challenges table the four answered rows have next step 'Không' and an empty owner; only the cache row is open ('chưa có số đo câu tìm lặp lại'), next step 'Đo sau khi có', owner Đội Cửa hàng.

ADR 0017 consequence: if shops need public product pages for search engines, they are HTML built on the server, separate from the app, decided in a separate ADR; ordering stays in the app. The HTML app-web returns for a product page does not contain the product name.
The review says public pages, if built, would read the same Catalog, and its 'ADR sẽ viết' section lists public product pages as a separate decision still to write under ADR 0017.

ADR 0030 consequences: no new copy; search shares the database with ordering, held by catalog-reads, ADR 0016 per-shop caps and the replica move per capacity-plan.md; no misspellings or synonyms; a shop moving under ADR 0026 takes its searchable words.
ADR 0030 reopen condition: misspelling or synonym complaints above 5% of search feedback in a month (assumed), or search load above the headroom even after moving to the replica.
ADR 0030 builds the searchable words from the product's own row (name lowercased, unaccented, split into words), so no separate copy exists.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0030 @ stage-4 'Quyết định'; product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 53

claims.text: ADR 0026: only DonHang.Api's database (donhang) moves shops out; from release 2 each request takes the shop from the access token and looks up its database in the shop map. Products live in donhang (review diagram).
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0026-cua-hang-lon-chuyen-sang-database-rieng.md @ stage-4 lines 36-44; product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 sơ đồ tổng thể

claims.text: Driver 3 of the search design: results only within the caller's shop; so one search reads one shop's rows, which after a move sit in one database.
ADR 0026 move condition (assumed): a shop moves when it holds more than 10% of total orders of the busiest day, or needs separate restore by contract.

Review risks table: how names with 'đ' normalise needs a separate check, owner Tester, add a test case when building; misspelling more than expected, owner Product owner (described as the role that sets product priorities), count search feedback monthly.

consistency-per-operation.md lets search be as old as the product list (new products found after a few minutes, assumed); capacity-plan.md allows the product list on the replica because of that tolerance.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/consistency-per-operation.md @ stage-4 line 15 (Tìm sản phẩm); docs/design/capacity-plan.md @ stage-4 'Đọc từ replica'

claims.text: Pointing to an accepted ADR is the honest answer only when the challenge neither changes a driver nor meets a reopen condition; when it brings new information (a contract, a count above the line), the decision is reopened with a new ADR.
A request to search across every shop's products contradicts driver 3, so it is a new requirement to take back to requirements, not a gap in this design.
An accepted ADR is not rewritten: when the decision changes, a new ADR records it and the old ADR's status only changes to 'Bị thay thế bởi NNNN'.

Search estimate (assumed): at most 5,000 products per shop, about 27 searches per second at the busiest hour, fits in PostgreSQL; a separate search engine is a copy fed from Catalog, with lag and a rebuild, not needed at that size.
